**Test image analysis:**
- Sugarcane plant with long narrow leaves
- One prominent leaf shows a distinct yellow/cream stripe running along the midrib/center length
- Rest of the leaf blade remains green; some brown dead lower leaves present
- No discrete spots, no mosaic pattern, no streaking across multiple veins

This midrib yellowing pattern strongly suggests **Yellow_Leaf** disease. Let me confirm with one reference image.

**Comparison:**
- Reference Yellow_Leaf shows more advanced/extensive yellowing and browning of the whole leaf
- Test image shows an earlier/milder stage: bright yellow midrib stripe with green leaf margins still intact
- Both have the same context (sugarcane field, similar dead lower leaves in background, same field conditions - likely same dataset)

The yellow midrib stripe in the test image is the hallmark symptom of Yellow Leaf disease (caused by Sugarcane yellow leaf virus), where midrib yellowing progresses before full leaf chlorosis occurs. The setting and leaf morphology match the Yellow_Leaf reference.

{"prediction": "Yellow_Leaf", "confidence": 0.78, "reasoning": "The test image shows a prominent yellow/cream stripe running along the midrib of a sugarcane leaf while the leaf blade margins remain green. This midrib yellowing is the defining early symptom of Yellow Leaf disease (ScYLV). The reference Yellow_Leaf image shows the same disease at a more advanced stage with extensive browning, consistent with progression from midrib yellowing. No discrete spots (rules out Brown_Spot/Yellow_Spot), no mosaic pattern (rules out Mosaic/Streak_Mosaic), no leaf margin scalding pattern (rules out Leaf_Scald)."}
